validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION: real, correctly classified intrastate gas transmission pipeline, confirmed independently of gem.wiki and of any GEM/GulfPub-style surface, via THREE independent origins that each name this specific pipeline (not a generic/aggregate mention): (1) World Pipelines trade press, 'Development of the Gemini Carthage Pipeline in Texas' (worldpipelines.com, dated 2018-12-28, url_verifier OK on 'Gemini Carthage'+'Harrison and Panola') — 'Gemini Midstream Holdings, LLC ... have announced the development of the Gemini Carthage Pipeline, a new natural gas system in Harrison and Panola Counties, Texas, capable of delivering in excess of 1.2 billion ft3/d of high pressure, dry natural gas'; (2) Trace Midstream press release PDF (tracemidstream.com, dated 2020-01-31; url_verifier's naive substring check FAILS on this PDF as a documented false negative — per url_verifier.py's own docstring on PDFs whose text stream the extractor can't fully read — so I downloaded it and confirmed by hand with `pdftotext -layout`: it names 'the Gemini Carthage Pipeline ("GCP"), an existing 50-mile natural gas system in Harrison and Panola Counties, Texas, capable of delivering in excess of 1.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d)' with 'initial in-service date of May 2019' and anchor producers Rockcliff Energy and Tanos Exploration); (3) Texas Railroad Commission's live 'Natural Gas Tariffs and Rate Schedules' filer list (rrc.texas.gov, page states 'Last updated on September 1st, 2026', url_verifier OK on 'GEMINI CARTHAGE') — an official, currently-active regulatory registry listing 'GEMINI CARTHAGE PIPELINE, LLC' as a 'Transmission' tariff filer (distinct from the separately listed 'GEMINI GULF COAST PIPELINE, LLC', GCP's sister project — no risk of the two being confused/conflated on this roster; GGCP is not itself a GEM row and is out of scope for this pass). RRC's CURRENT listing also confirms Status=operating is still true today, not just as of the 2018-2020 sources. CLASSIFICATION: RRC's own 'Transmission' designation (as opposed to 'Distribution' or a gathering-only filer) matches treating this as a transmission trunk, not a gathering/feeder line, even though GEM's PipelineType cell is currently blank (deep-filled below). Fuel=Gas confirmed by both (1) and (2) ('natural gas system', 'dry natural gas'). Location (StartLocation=Harrison County / EndLocation=Panola County, Texas) confirmed verbatim by both (1) and (2). DUPLICATE CHECK against the 45-row Texas roster: no other row describes this Harrison–Panola County corridor or a 'Carthage'-named system; not a relabel/segment double-count of any other PID on the list. Opened all 4 harvested wiki citations for this row: worldpipelines.com (live, cited), geminimidstream.com/gcp (ConnectionError live AND on Wayback — web.archive.org content-serving was unreachable from this session all day, a known network condition per project history, not evidence the capture doesn't exist; not cited, no fabricated substitute), rrc.texas.gov general tariff page (live, cited, and it independently corroborates far more — the exact entity name — than the generic tariff-schedule context the wiki citation implied), and the tracemidstream.com PDF (live per curl 200, content hand-verified via pdftotext, cited despite the verifier's PDF-extraction false negative).

validity.recommendation: no change; note that the sourced figure is a floor ('in excess of'), not an exact nameplate spec
validity.researcher_notes: CAPACITY: GEM's 12.40 bcm/y converts to exactly 1.2 bcf/d (1.2 bcf/d × 365 d/y × 0.0283168 bcm/bcf ≈ 12.40 bcm/y), which is precisely the figure both independent sources give — World Pipelines (2018, pre-construction) and Trace Midstream (2020, post in-service) both say the system is 'capable of delivering in excess of 1.2 billion [cubic feet/ft3] per day.' Both sources use 'in excess of,' i.e. a stated floor rather than an exact nameplate number, so GEM's 12.40 is a reasonable rounding of the sourced figure but is technically a minimum, not a precise capacity spec. Not material enough to recommend a change — flagging as a caveat only. StartYear1=2019 is corroborated by both sources agreeing on the year (World Pipelines projected 1Q19 operational in its 2018 forecast; Trace's 2020 release gives the confirmed actual 'initial in-service date of May 2019') — the 1Q19-forecast-vs-May-2019-actual gap is normal project-timeline slip, not a conflict, and StartMonth1=5 is now deep-filled from the Trace release (see fills[]).
